title: Won on price, then paid more than the runner-up offered
question: Where the lowest bidder won, has the City since paid more than the second-lowest bidder asked?
finding: Of 39 matched contracts won by the lowest bidder where the second bid is known, payments already exceed the second-lowest bid on 3: Bay Area Lightworks Inc, PW Cntrt No.36 Trffc Sgnl Mod (Public Works): bid $3.4 million, next bid $4.4 million, paid $5.7 million; Hoseley Corporation, PRT CT2786 P94 BACKLANDS (Port): bid $6.7 million, next bid $6.8 million, paid $7.5 million; Chiang C.M. Construction Inc, PW SF RENT BOARD TNNT IMPR (Public Works): bid $1.4 million, next bid $1.5 million, paid $1.6 million. On 6 more the ceiling, which includes contingency the contractor may never be paid, stands above the second bid. Together the 3 were paid $2.2 million more than the runner-up's price.
how: Rows of the low-bid screen in the site’s “Over budget and late” page (each published bid sheet matched to its contract in the Supplier Contracts table) where the lowest bidder holds the contract. The second-lowest bid is the winning bid times one plus the margin on the sheet; it is compared with payments to date and with the present ceiling.
limits: A change order pays for work that was not in the bid documents, and the runner-up would have been paid for the same added work, so paying more than the second bid does not show the award was wrong. Unit-price paving contracts are paid on measured quantities. The test is whether the added work was foreseeable when bids were taken, which needs the change-order files. Only 54 of 98 bid sheets could be matched to a contract.
